subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory contract, by Memory Wiki as a knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the request defines durable memory schema, conflict policy, provenance semantics, and operator UX, so automation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core or the active memory plugin API as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, claims, source evidence, and entity normalization as Memory Wiki responsibilities while memory-core remains Markdown/search/promotion.

options.title: Defer to plugin experiments
options.body: Use ClawHub smart-memory and production-agent implementations as design input before accepting durable schema or UX commitments in core.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core or the active memory plugin API as the owning contract for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history around the memory plugin slot, Memory Wiki direction, and plugin/core boundary decisions.
